2022 was a significant year for ideological filmmaking. Disney and Pixar doubled down on progressive content in their animated slate. Marvel's woke era reached peak density. Netflix delivered one of the most politically coded prestige films in recent memory. And Olivia Wilde made a movie explicitly inspired by Jordan Peterson.

This list ranks the 10 most ideologically progressive films released in 2022 using the VirtueVigil Woke Score methodology. Every film here has been reviewed in full on VirtueVigil with detailed trope-by-trope breakdowns. The rankings run from #10 to #1. Scores reflect the density of progressive ideological content as measured by our scoring system, not artistic merit or entertainment value.

These scores complete the VirtueVigil annual rankings series: 2024, 2023, and now 2022 are all documented. You can compare the patterns across years and see how Hollywood's ideological priorities shifted over time.

#10 - The Menu (2022)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 9.3 • Verdict: MIXED • Score Margin: 0 NEUTRAL

Mark Mylod's class satire targets wealthy elites, food culture pretension, and the commodification of art with equal contempt for all sides. The film's anti-capitalist streak is real and deliberate, but its contempt for status-obsessed critics and wealthy consumers reads as conservative instinct as much as progressive rage. Ralph Fiennes' chef is as contemptuous of progressive cultural gatekeepers as he is of old money. The cheeseburger that saves the day is the film's clearest ideological statement: earnestness defeats pretension. The scores nearly cancel out because the rage is bipartisan. The Menu lands on this list at #10 because the anti-capitalist framework earns it a marginal woke edge, but it is a film that genuinely defies easy categorization.

#9 - Amsterdam (2022)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 10.49 • Verdict: MIXED • Score Margin: -1 WOKE

David O. Russell assembled one of the most impressive casts of 2022 for a story based on a real 1933 conspiracy in which American industrialists allegedly tried to recruit a retired general to lead a fascist coup against FDR. The anti-fascist messaging is explicit, the framing of the villains as ideologically adjacent to contemporary populism is deliberate, and the film draws a clear line between historical fascism and modern political movements. Traditional elements including male friendship, loyalty, and wartime heroism exist in tension with the political subtext, which is why the scores nearly tie. It lands on this list because the political framing of its villains drives the woke margin above neutral, but just barely.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Amsterdam

#8 - Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 13.6 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Score Margin: -3 WOKE

Sam Raimi brought genuine horror filmmaking to the MCU and Elizabeth Olsen delivered a career-best performance as the Scarlet Witch. Underneath the craft is a film that introduces America Chavez wearing a pride flag patch, features an alternate Earth where Captain America is a woman and Captain Marvel is Black, and uses a teenage girl as the franchise's moral center while Strange repeatedly fails or causes harm. The Illuminati sequence is a referendum on male superhero authority. Raimi's directorial discipline keeps the ideology from overwhelming the story, but VirtueVigil's trope audit identifies consistent progressive content layered throughout the multiverse's design choices and character framing.

#7 - Lightyear (2022)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 10.22 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Score Margin: -4 WOKE

Pixar's Buzz Lightyear origin film became a political flashpoint when its same-sex kiss scene was restored after initially being removed from the cut. Fourteen countries banned the film over the content. Alisha Hawthorne's lesbian relationship and family are normalized as a core story element, with the time-jump structure making her wife and children recurring supporting characters. Pixar confirmed the decision to include the relationship was intentional and deliberate. The film itself is a mediocre sci-fi adventure that did not earn the controversy it generated, but the ideological decision to make the same-sex relationship a plot-driving element earns its place in the top 10.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Lightyear

#6 - Thor: Love and Thunder (2022)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 16.44 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Score Margin: -4 WOKE

Taika Waititi hands Thor's hammer to Jane Foster and spends two hours systematically dismantling every traditionally masculine element the character ever had. Thor is feminized, mocked, and sidelined in his own film. The Zeus scene codes traditional male authority as cartoonishly corrupt and self-serving. Jane Foster's Thor arc is the explicit message: the female successor is morally superior to the original. Christian Bale's Gorr the God Butcher contains genuine pathos that a more disciplined film would have built around. Instead, those tragic elements are buried under rainbow goats, fourth-wall comedy, and franchise obligations that drain the story of any weight it earns.

#5 - Black Panther: Wakanda Forever (2022)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 18.42 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Score Margin: -6 WOKE

Ryan Coogler's sequel weaves in the Ironheart setup, Namor's indigenous liberation narrative, and Shuri's revenge arc into a film that is genuinely moving when it stays focused on grief and legacy. But the ideological freight is significant: Namor's entire motivation is anti-colonial liberation from Western imperialism, Riri Williams' introduction is a diversity-mandate setup for a spinoff series, and Shuri's arc explicitly frames revenge over forgiveness as the more honest path. Angela Bassett's performance as Queen Ramonda is one of the best in the MCU's history. The film around her is too burdened with franchise obligations and progressive signaling to fully honor it.

#4 - Turning Red (2022)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 17.85 • Verdict: WOKE • Score Margin: -13 WOKE

Pixar's puberty allegory is technically brilliant and emotionally effective, which makes its ideological content all the more potent. The film's central thesis is direct: traditional parenting, cultural expectations, and parental authority are the primary sources of a young girl's suffering. The mother's values are presented as trauma-inducing control. Family loyalty and tradition are positioned as obstacles to authentic self-expression. VirtueVigil's trope audit identifies consistent subversion of traditional family structures throughout, with religious and cultural values coded as harmful and the authority figures who enforce them as the story's true antagonists. Pixar made it beautiful and moving, which is exactly what makes it effective.

#3 - Strange World (2022)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 27.5 • Verdict: WOKE • Score Margin: -15 WOKE

Disney went full ideological accelerator with Strange World and the box office reflected it. A $180 million animated film about a family of explorers who discover their miracle energy source is actually a parasitic infection killing a living ecosystem, featuring Disney's first openly gay animated lead character. The environmental metaphor is not subtext: Pando is fossil fuel, Avalonia is industrial civilization, and the solution is to stop using energy and live in harmony with the planet. The openly gay character, Ethan Clyde-Lightfoot, is written without comment or announcement, which is how Disney signals normalization rather than celebration. The film lost an estimated $197 million. Sometimes the market provides feedback.

#2 - Don't Worry Darling (2022)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 21.84 • Verdict: WOKE • Score Margin: -19 WOKE

Olivia Wilde's feminist thriller uses a 1950s utopia to construct a sustained attack on traditional gender roles, male authority, and domestic life as a form of women's imprisonment. The villain is explicitly inspired by Jordan Peterson, a detail Wilde confirmed in interviews, framing the male lead as an ideologue who traps women in a domestic fantasy against their will. Every visual of domestic comfort is deliberately reframed as a prison by the film's conclusion. Florence Pugh's performance transcends the material. The film's woke score of 21.84 reflects a systematic ideological framework that leaves no traditional value unexamined and no male authority unimplicated. One of the most agenda-driven films of 2022.

#1 - Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery (2022)

VirtueVigil Woke Score: 42 • Verdict: STRONGLY WOKE • Score Margin: -24 WOKE

Rian Johnson's Netflix sequel is the most ideologically dense film of 2022 by a significant margin. The woke score of 42 is the highest of any 2022 release VirtueVigil reviewed. Miles Bron is a thinly veiled composite of tech billionaire culture and MAGA political sensibility, and the film's thesis is that such figures succeed not through intelligence but through the willingness of their enablers to pretend they are smart. The film's entire structure is a class warfare argument: Bron is stupid and dangerous, his orbit is complicit, and the only moral actor is a woman of color whose loyalty he betrayed. The mystery mechanics work. The ideology is the film's reason for existing.

How 2022 Compares

The highest woke score in 2022 was 42 (Glass Onion). For comparison, 2024's highest was 42.6 (Conclave) and 2023's top entry was also in the low-to-mid 40s. The density of ideological content in mainstream releases has been consistent across these three years. What changed was the genre distribution: in 2022, animation and superhero films dominated this list. By 2024, prestige drama and horror had taken over. Hollywood's progressive messaging migrated from family-friendly content toward adult awards-bait between 2022 and 2024.

Notably, 2022's list includes four Disney/Pixar animated films in the top 10 (Strange World, Turning Red, Lightyear, plus Thor from Marvel). That concentration of ideological content in family-targeted animated releases was a deliberate strategic choice by Disney leadership that has since been reversed under current leadership following significant box office pressure.

Methodology Note

All scores are generated using the VirtueVigil Woke Score system, which measures the density and intensity of progressive ideological content across multiple categories including gender politics, religious critique, racial messaging, sexual content framing, and institutional critique. The system does not measure quality, entertainment value, or artistic merit. For full details, visit our Methodology page.

This list reflects films reviewed by VirtueVigil as of March 2026. All scores are final once published and are not adjusted retroactively.
